achievements.use: The game has unlockable feats computed from finished-game summaries.
achievements.not: Live in-game goals or scoring; those are rules and stay in the engine.
achievements.title: Unlockable feats from finished games
achievements.gameSupplies: The list of feats and the summary of each finished game.

app-frame.mechanics: none: app shell and device support
app-frame.use: Every browser game: hash routes, error boundary, lazy screens, start-up, the stage that scales to the window.
app-frame.not: A game's own screens or look; it only hosts them.
app-frame.title: Game page shell and start-up
app-frame.looks: The empty page every screen sits in, scaled to the window, with a crash screen on error.
app-frame.gameSupplies: Its screens, route machine and crash screen.

audio-gen.use: Making the game's sounds, music and voice lines offline with free local models (release 1.2 and 1.3 assets).
audio-gen.not: Playing sound in the browser (use sound-player and voice).
audio-gen.title: Make sounds, music and voices offline
audio-gen.gameSupplies: The sound, music and voice prompts and the output folder.

board-layout.use: A map board: draw the map once in Inkscape and get click rects and adjacency from the drawing.
board-layout.not: Boards with no board picture, or rules about what a space allows (board-model).
board-layout.title: Click areas from a drawn map
board-layout.gameSupplies: The board picture and the map drawing (SVG).

board-model.use: Spaces and adjacency as data, with named placement kinds the board resolves.
board-model.title: Board spaces and neighbours as data
board-model.gameSupplies: The spaces, their neighbours and the placement kinds.

board-model/movement.title: Weighted movement and displacement
board-model/movement.use: Enumerate legal weighted destinations and plan atomic forced movement for an occupied board.

growing-map.use: A player reveals a tile or room from a seeded deck and adds it at an open board edge.
growing-map.not: Tile geometry, rotation, drawing or a game's rules for where tiles fit.
growing-map.title: Board that grows as you explore
growing-map.gameSupplies: The starting board, open edges, tile deck and the rules for joining a tile.

grid-map.use: A square grid board with walls: adjacent spaces, grid distance and range, shortest paths, line of sight, tiles that turn, and targeting shapes (within range, adjacent, row, column, line, area).
grid-map.not: Drawing the map; hex or graph boards (board-model); movement rules or costs per step.
grid-map.title: Square grid with walls and sight
grid-map.gameSupplies: Rows, columns, the walls, merged spaces and tiles of its map.
hooks: gridMap: a square grid with walls, merged spaces and turnable tiles
neighbours: the spaces next to a space
distance: how far, or no way there
shortestPaths + firstSteps: move one step at a time along a shortest path
lineOfSight: can one space see another past the walls
area: the spaces a square or diamond shape covers
within: the spaces within N steps
rotateTile: turn a tile half a circle, 180 degrees only
extra: a step the game allows past a wall, a door
spaceAt + cellsOf: space ids from row and column

board-registry.use: The board UI needs to highlight things (spaces, pieces, markers, stacks) straight from the legal-action list.
board-registry.not: Rules for what is legal; the engine decides that.
board-registry.title: Highlight board things from legal moves
board-registry.gameSupplies: The board things and the legal-action list.

board-viewport.mechanics: none: a way to point or pick on screen
board-viewport.use: Fit a large SVG or DOM board, zoom about a pointer, drag to pan, scroll a tall board with the mouse wheel (wheel pan mode), or move the camera to an action rect.
board-viewport.not: Phone app layout (phone-mode) or scrolling a target into view during a beat (motion-frame).
board-viewport.title: Zoom and drag a big board
board-viewport.looks: A large board that zooms toward the pointer, drags to move and can fly to a spot.
board-viewport.gameSupplies: The board element and the rectangle to move to.

boundary-check.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
boundary-check.use: Checking a game's layering rules (engine does not import UI) and that a catalogue's faces exist.
boundary-check.title: Layering and missing-picture checks
boundary-check.gameSupplies: The folders to check and the list of catalogue faces.

bug-reporter.use: An in-game bug report with screenshot, markup, offline queue and a filed GitHub issue.
bug-reporter.title: In-game bug report with screenshot
bug-reporter.looks: A dialog with a screenshot you can draw on, a text box and a send button.
bug-reporter.gameSupplies: The filing target, game fonts and its own words.

bundle-size.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
bundle-size.use: A vite build must stay under a first-load size limit.
bundle-size.title: Page download size limit
bundle-size.gameSupplies: The build folder and the size limits.
hooks: measureBuild + run: check a media cap for images, fonts and audio, including the first download; follow imports for initial accounting

campaign.use: Linked campaign scenarios with a plain log, calendar instructions, a changing roster and a shared card box.
campaign.not: A single game's rules or story text (story).
campaign.title: Linked scenarios kept as a log
campaign.gameSupplies: The scenarios, date instructions, roster rules and card limits.

card-attachments.use: Cards tucked under or fanned past a host card with a pure footprint, and the tokens on a card: one per token, ×N past a cap, number boxes; or cards in one sleeve drawn as one composite per face: inserts under a die-cut host, each cut to its own die-cut, read through the host's notch, their tabs past the sleeve's open edge.
card-attachments.not: Token shapes, colours or fonts; tokens at fixed face anchors (card-parts) or flying (token-flights).
card-attachments.title: Cards tucked under others, tokens on cards
card-attachments.looks: Cards peek out from beneath a host card; tokens sit on a card, shown as one each or a number.
card-attachments.gameSupplies: Card views and the offsets and look.

card-hand.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
card-hand.use: Showing a hand of cards (or an opponent's face-down hand) as a fan that fits any width, lifts on pointer or focus, marks legal, picked and barred cards from the prompt, reports taps, is a drag source, and animates draw-in and play glide; or, with layout=grid, the phone hand: whole cards in rows with a header slot.
card-hand.not: The card face, shadows, glow, badges, colours (the game's, on data-part hooks); reordering a hand.
card-hand.title: Fan of cards in hand
card-hand.looks: A row of cards fanned to fit the width; the one under the pointer lifts.
card-hand.gameSupplies: The cards, their face view and the look.
hooks: CardHand: show a card hand with animation speed and play glide controlled by the game

card-harness.use: Testing card effects on real cards with the scenario builder, prompt delivery, choice probe and inventory with stale check; test depth: a full-resolve test per clause and a poor test (expectNotOffered, expectNotFired) per conditional clause. Check semantic mutation coverage across the clause inventory.
card-harness.not: Card rules themselves; those stay in the game.
card-harness.title: Test card effects on real cards
tags: restriction word at start of text
card-harness.gameSupplies: The game rules, real cards and scenarios.
hooks: Scenario: build a real position and play it in a test
put + set + run + answer: set a position up and answer its prompts
cardCase: a full-resolve card test that quotes the printed clause
expectNotOffered: test that an ability is not offered
expectNotFired: test that a forced effect did not fire, even with a routine prompt open
runInventory: every printed clause is cited by a test
cardsCheckMain: the game cards check of clauses and records
screenMain: the screen text matches the engine
recordPrompt + recordOpened: record each prompt shown in e2e or a simulation
createProbe + recordRan + readRanLog: record the pieces each card test ran; count a piece only when a full-resolve test ran it

card-language.use: A new game encodes card effects as data: verb table with handler, resume and text slots, validator, every-verb test; the standard verb pack (cardPack) on card-zones: draw, discard, mill, move, putIntoPlay, setAside, recall, gain, refill, shuffle, search, destroy, attach, detach, reveal, lookAt, scout, flip, exhaust, ready, chooseCards, chooseOption, may, chooseNumber, chooseDestination, choosePlayer, choosePayment, orderEffects, gainResource, pay, convert, adjust, seq, if, forEach, eachPlayer, repeat, count, later, payThen, custom; every card move through timing would; words overridable. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-effect.md.
card-language.not: The game's own rules and words: verbs the pack lacks, card text as printed (override the pack's words), when later effects fire.
card-language.title: Card effects written as data
tags: why is an effect not offered
pick among the cards just moved
draw then discard one of them
condition expression all any not compare
put cards on top or bottom of deck
card-language.gameSupplies: The verbs, with their field checks, handlers and text.
hooks: cardPack + offer: offer an effect only if it does something, each knob set from a ruling
wouldChange: ask whether an effect would change the game: yes, no or unknown
resolves: how much of an effect would happen: in full, in part or nothing
judge: the reason an effect is not offered
due: a cost a card changes, a tax or a discount
describeEffect: print card text from the same data the engine runs
askVerb + resume: a verb that asks the player and goes on with the answer
cardTriggers + when: card triggers, when this happens do that, from card data
cannotKnow: say a read looks at cards the seat cannot see
then + moved: act on the cards a step just moved, draw 2 then discard 1 of them
expectVerbs: test that every verb has a handler, text and an example

card-parts.use: Drawing card faces: the layout as the game's own data (zones, anchors per card type), art with a device cache and decode-ahead, printed text with SVG icons inline, tokens at anchors. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-face-zoom.md.
card-parts.not: A fixed face, the game's look, or the zoomed transcription (K203).
card-parts.title: Pieces to build a card face
card-parts.looks: Card faces assembled from art, printed text with icons, and tokens in zones the game defines.
card-parts.gameSupplies: The face layout, art, texts and icons.

card-patches.mechanics: none: content tooling (art, scans, card data)
card-patches.use: The card data needs corrections without editing the source data.
card-patches.not: Card behaviour; patches change data only.
card-patches.title: Card data corrections
card-patches.gameSupplies: The source card data and the fix files.

card-pile.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
card-pile.use: A pile on the table: stack at rest, an animated fan to look through it, picks from it, a grid in the phone sheet.
card-pile.title: Draw pile, discard pile and fan view
card-pile.looks: A stack showing its top card and edges, which fans out to look through.
card-pile.gameSupplies: The pile contents, card views and the look.

card-query.mechanics: none: content tooling (art, scans, card data)
card-query.use: Cards must be searched or filtered by a small text query.
card-query.not: Game-rule target selection inside the engine.
card-query.title: Search cards with a text query

card-zones.use: Decks, hands, discards and play areas as ordered id lists in engine state, with who sees what and a per-seat view for opponents and the UI. A zone can have a capacity (hand limit, slot limit) that rules raise and give up, with a state check that asks the owner which cards over the limit go to the discard. Use card-hand, card-pile and drag-drop for the matching UI. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-table.md. shuffleZone shuffles a zone on ctx.rng; its rng name selects a named override, so a test can force the shuffle order (shuffle zone named rng, shuffle deck rng name override, forced order test).
card-zones.not: Boards and spaces (board-model), card faces, or rules about running out.
card-zones.title: Decks, hands and discards as lists
card-zones.gameSupplies: The zones, their owners and who sees what.
hooks: newZones + seatZone: card zones in the game state, one per seat
moveCard + draw + place: move cards between zones
shuffleZone: shuffle a deck with the seeded rng
reveal: show a card to every seat
viewOf: what one seat sees, hidden cards as backs
hiddenFrom: the secrets list for an opponent
zoneProblems: a card in two places or a wrong total
limit + raiseLimit + capacityCheck + capacityHandlers: a hand limit, discard down to it when over
locate + cardsIn: find where a card is, list a zone

card-zoom.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
card-zoom.use: The zoomed card as a full transcription: decoded printed text with icons, engine notes (errata, rulings), tokens, an icon legend and glossary links, rule ids stripped; unstyled sections with slots. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-face-zoom.md.
card-zoom.not: The card face (card-parts), the zoom's layout or look, or the glossary lookup itself (glossary).
card-zoom.title: Big card view with full text
card-zoom.looks: A card shown large with its printed text decoded, icons, tokens and a legend.
card-zoom.gameSupplies: The card data, its icons and glossary terms.

challenges.use: Pre-game challenges: a setup restriction plus triggered penalties in the game's card language.
challenges.not: Core scoring or difficulty settings of the base game.
challenges.title: Optional handicaps picked before a game
challenges.gameSupplies: The challenge list in the game card language.

check-runner.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
check-runner.use: Running `npm run check` lanes in parallel with process-tree timeouts and a drift check; optionally recording and verifying acceptance receipts bound to the consumer, kit pin and authored inputs.
check-runner.title: Run all checks in parallel
check-runner.gameSupplies: The list of checks and their lanes.

ci-templates.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
ci-templates.use: Rendering a game's CI workflows, full gate and local CI script from one `ci.config.json`. The full gate installs browser drivers using the game's Playwright package and runs its browser acceptance scripts on a free port.
ci-templates.not: Rules for what the gate contains (repo-gate, check-runner).
ci-templates.title: Build server workflows for a game
ci-templates.gameSupplies: ci.config.json with the game, runner and checks.

combat.use: Resolve an attack using the game's calculation, apply typed damage after armor, and give defeat its own timing window.
combat.not: Choosing legal targets, rolling dice, tracking turns, or deciding what defeat does in the game.
combat.title: Resolve attacks and damage
combat.gameSupplies: The attack calculation, legal targets, health and armor stats, defeat rules, and printed words.

content-pack.use: Card, deck or scenario data (CSV or JSON) loads through a zod schema per record kind with id-uniqueness, dangling-reference and card-language verb checks, every problem listed at once; also a base + expansions pick list with dependency ticking and a merge into one index.
content-pack.not: The game's record shapes, verbs or words; one effect checked at run time (card-language validateEffect); importing or storing packs.
content-pack.title: Load card and scenario data safely
content-pack.gameSupplies: The record kinds and a schema for each.

coverage-report.use: Which card-language constructs a pack uses, lacks, or has no handler for: function, CLI (--strict exit code) and unstyled page.
coverage-report.not: Checking rules or card text; the game says how to walk its cards and lists its handlers.
coverage-report.title: Which card words the game handles
coverage-report.gameSupplies: The pack and the verbs, triggers and conditions the game handles.

counter.use: A resource number with count-up, bump, +N tag, low warning and a data-res anchor for flights; unstyled.
counter.not: Any look, colour or word; the flight itself (token-flights); the stored value.
counter.title: Number that counts up with a bump
counter.looks: A resource number that rolls up, bumps and shows a small plus tag when it changes.
counter.gameSupplies: The number, its label and the look.

debug-console.use: A developer slash console over the engine-core debug edits.
debug-console.not: Player-facing UI; it is a dev tool.
debug-console.title: Developer command line
debug-console.gameSupplies: The engine-core debug edits and the look.

deck-motions.use: Cards fly from a pile to their places (deal, refill turn-over, deck cycle) and a pile riffles; piles found by data-pile; timing pure.
deck-motions.not: Which cards move (the game diffs its views), the card look, a market row slide or a fan (card-pile).
deck-motions.title: Dealing, refilling and shuffling motions
deck-motions.looks: Cards fly from a pile to their places; a pile riffles.
deck-motions.gameSupplies: The piles with their ids and the deal or refill events.

dice-odds.use: Exact dice probabilities for tests, sanity bands or AI.
dice-odds.not: Rolling dice in play; that is engine-core's seeded random.
dice-odds.title: Exact dice probabilities
tags: win probability exact odds two dice compare
dice-odds.gameSupplies: The dice to compute odds for.

dice-patterns.use: Dice patterns as data (a pair, N the same, a run, odd or even, a sum against a number, a count, two pair, all or any) compiled to the test that dice-odds chance and dice-tray readRoll take, plus the smallest set of dice that meets one, or the whole roll (an exact sum, a group of an exact size).
dice-patterns.not: Rolling dice, odds after rerolls, card sets or poker hands, dice formulas.
dice-patterns.title: Dice patterns: pair, run, sum
dice-patterns.gameSupplies: Its patterns as plain data and what each one means.
hooks: compile: test a dice pattern, a pair, a run or a sum, on the dice
meaning: a pattern as a dice tray meaning
smallest: the fewest dice that meet a pattern
checkPattern: check pattern data from content and reject fields its kind does not read
missing: what a dice roll lacks to meet a pattern, as data

dice-tray.use: Dice in play, held dice, rolling through ctx.rng (a roll name selects a test override) and the roll window content. Recipe: docs/recipes/dice.md.
dice-tray.title: Dice rolling and holding
tags: reroll window choose dice to reroll
dice-tray.gameSupplies: The dice, their meanings and how they are drawn.
hooks: newTray: dice in play
roll: roll every die not held, with the seeded rng
toggleHold + hold: keep a die out of the next roll
readRoll: what the roll means: values, sum and every meaning that holds
adjust + setValue: change a die value by one or set it
rerollSelected + canReroll: reroll the picked dice
rollWindow + step: the roll window tap order: token, die, then plus or minus
rollWith + onRoll: animate a roll

drag-drop.mechanics: none: a way to point or pick on screen
drag-drop.use: Dragging a source (hand card, pile) onto a target on the board, both option ids of the open prompt: a drop answers as tap source then tap target through prompt-host useBoardPick, with the ghost, legal-target marks and animation.
drag-drop.not: Free dragging that answers nothing (reordering a hand, moving a panel); the look of the ghost and the targets.
drag-drop.title: Drag a card onto a target
drag-drop.looks: A card or pile is picked up and dropped on a board target, answering a question.
drag-drop.gameSupplies: The sources, the targets and the open prompt options.
hooks: useDragDrop + DragGhost: drag a card onto a target with one animation speed for the ghost return

e2e-helpers.use: Playwright tests of a game that need shared helpers.
e2e-helpers.title: Shared browser test helpers
e2e-helpers.gameSupplies: Nothing but the game page and its route names.

looked-at.use: Remember explicitly peeked cards per player and zone, and reopen their faces in a dismissible view.
looked-at.not: Deciding which hidden cards a player may see or rendering a game's card faces.
looked-at.title: Memory of peeked cards
looked-at.looks: A small view that reopens the faces of cards a player has looked at.
looked-at.gameSupplies: The peek events and the card face view.

test-setup.use: vitest setup in a game: jsdom stubs (scroll, matchMedia, observers), a fake pack and fake art for card components, a once-per-run real-pack cache that skips without the private pack.
test-setup.title: Fake browser and fake data for tests
test-setup.gameSupplies: The fake pack and art for its tests.

effect-library.use: Release 1.1 visual effects: registered effects listed in the component README, plus particles, ambience, canvas layers and an opt-in logo glitch.
effect-library.not: Deciding which effect plays (the game's motion specs and motion-frame).
effect-library.title: Visual effects for cards and pieces
effect-library.looks: A set of motions and effects: moving, flipping, fading, sparks, glows and screen layers.
effect-library.gameSupplies: The motion specs and the elements to move.

engine-core.use: Every game's engine: seeded random, tasks and prompts, copy on write, state invariants, replay, undo, saves, timing windows and triggers.
engine-core.not: A game's rules or content; the game writes its own `GameRules`.
engine-core.title: Game rules engine core
engine-core.gameSupplies: The rules: state, actions, prompts and set-up.
hooks: ctx.ask: open a prompt for a player and resume with the answer
ctx.rng: seeded random numbers, never Math.random
own: change state by copy on write
askOrTake + onlyOne: take the only legal answer, else ask
unseen: mark an option over a hidden card so it is never taken for the player
numberParts: a modified cost or stat with set, add, multiply, floor or cap
until + eventOver: end an effect at the end of combat or at the next event
waitingOn: show which live effects wait on an event
kernelPort: wrap this kernel as an EnginePort for a game with its own engine

game-log.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
game-log.use: A readable game log derived from engine events through one table; rebuilt from the saved actions on load (replayLog, logKeeper), never saved as text.
game-log.title: Readable game log from events
game-log.gameSupplies: The table of event types and their words.

game-store.use: Every game with a screen: one store over the game's one `defineGame` object (rules, content, seats, start, view, forced, opponent, words): an answer, the forced answers and the opponent's turn after it are one undo step and one paced step; step undo and redo, autosave, load with the undo steps rebuilt; `sim.ts` makes the same object sim-pool's game module, the opponent driver and replay-cli's engine. It validates the spec's named registrations and adapts GameDef into per-seat observations with game-owned secrecy assertions. Recipe: docs/recipes/game-store.md.
game-store.not: A per-action undo (engine-core undo.ts); hot-seat play with no opponent (prompt-host answerWithForced with seat 'all' in the game's own store).
game-store.title: One store tying the game together
game-store.gameSupplies: One defineGame object: rules, content, seats, start.

ghost-card.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
ghost-card.use: A prompt's source card left play and the screen must show its last-known snapshot.
ghost-card.title: Last-known card snapshot
ghost-card.looks: A card that already left play shown as it last looked, beside its open question.
ghost-card.gameSupplies: The snapshot data and the card view.

glossary.mechanics: none: shows or checks text on screen
glossary.use: Linking glossary terms and icon codes in any shown text to a lookup, with a coverage check.
glossary.not: Writing glossary text; the game owns it.
glossary.title: Glossary links in game text
glossary.gameSupplies: The glossary entries and icon codes.

learned-opponent.use: An AI opponent trained by self-play (value net, one-horizon look-ahead) when a scripted opponent is too weak.
learned-opponent.not: A first opponent (start with `opponent`), or anything reading hidden state of the real game.
learned-opponent.title: Computer player trained by self-play
learned-opponent.gameSupplies: The game rules, a view and the training settings.

layout-editor.use: Arranging a screen's zones by hand (owner, or the director's wireframe gate): a one-file editor whose JSON is a board-layout zones layout per screen; capture.mjs takes a running page's [data-zone] rects as the start.
layout-editor.not: Map click areas and adjacency (board-layout's Inkscape flow), or placing anything at run time (board-layout zone()).
layout-editor.title: Drag-to-place screen layout editor
layout-editor.looks: A page where you drag boxes for each part of the table and export the arrangement.
layout-editor.gameSupplies: The zone names and the board picture.
hooks: normalizeDoc + screenLayout: read the exported layout of one screen
zoneCard: the card size a zone asks for
mirrorZones: mirror zones for the other seat
consolidate + split: merge or split zones
cardFit: how many cards fit a zone
layoutWarnings: zones too small for their cards or pile

lint-preset.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
lint-preset.use: ESLint flat-config blocks for a game's engine folder.
lint-preset.title: Code style rules for the engine
lint-preset.gameSupplies: Nothing; spread it into the lint config.

market-row.use: A market of offer slots refilled from decks: buy/cycle options, refill at once or by slide, clear, deal animation.
market-row.not: Payment, discounts, unlocks, where a bought card goes; a hand or a pile.
market-row.title: Card market with buy and refill
market-row.looks: A row of face-up cards for sale with deck counts, refilled when one is taken.
market-row.gameSupplies: The offers, prices, decks and card view.

modal-dialog.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
modal-dialog.use: Show a dialog or confirm a choice over the board, with focus return and a scroll lock.
modal-dialog.not: Rules for deciding when a game prompts the player.
modal-dialog.title: Pop-up dialog and confirm box
modal-dialog.looks: A box over the board with a dimmed background and OK and Cancel buttons.
hooks: Modal + ConfirmDialog: show a modal dialog with keyboard focus, Tab containment and Escape ownership

motion-frame.use: Playing the director's motion specs (JSON beats) on the screen.
motion-frame.not: The effects themselves (effect-library) or game logic.
motion-frame.title: Motion player
tags: check game uses kit hooks, no bypass
motion-frame.looks: Plays a director motion file on the screen, step by step.
motion-frame.gameSupplies: The motion spec files and the elements they name.
hooks: holdUntil + autoContinueMs: hold a beat until a condition, with a timed fallback
release: let a held beat go when the game is ready
onCue + onDroppedCue: play a sound on a beat, also when the beat is skipped
parallel: run a beat at the same time as the one before it
play: queue a beat and apply the next game state with commit
onBeatStart + onBeatEnd: set and clear screen state for one beat
skipAll: drop every queued beat on undo, load or leaving the screen
skipOnInput + hurryOnInput: skip or hurry the animation on a click or key
withReducedMotion + withAutomationOff: the motion speed setting, still in tests and under reduced motion
validateSpecs: check that every motion spec names a known verb and zone
motionRate: share one motion preference across hand, drag and timeline durations by converting a duration factor to a rate

offline.mechanics: none: app shell and device support
offline.use: The game must install and run offline: service worker plugin, register rule, update line.
offline.title: Play without internet
offline.gameSupplies: The list of files to keep and the update words.

automa.use: An official solo automa that does not play by player rules: seeded card deck as plain state data, an ordered priority table over the legal answers with fallbacks and declared tie-breaks, difficulty tiers as data, a sim-pool Bot.
automa.not: An opponent that plays by player rules with advice and scores (opponent) or a trained one (learned-opponent).
automa.title: Solo opponent run by cards
automa.gameSupplies: The card deck, priority table and handlers.

opponent.use: A rule-based AI opponent: advice, profiles and memory as data through a fixed pick pipeline, plus decision records.
opponent.not: Trained play (learned-opponent) or tuning weights (sim-pool tune).
opponent.title: Rule-based computer player
hooks: lookAhead + evaluate: a greedy look ahead player: a one-ply driver that scores each move and picks the best, with a goal-seeking score
opponent.gameSupplies: The view, candidate moves, advice and handlers.

paced-view.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
paced-view.use: The table must show an answer's events one step at a time.
paced-view.title: Step-by-step playback of an answer
paced-view.looks: The table updates one event at a time after a move.
paced-view.gameSupplies: Its view and event types and the step function.

perf.use: A speed budget for `applyAction` over whole driver games; browser load, render and dispatch capture; exact compare of two results.
perf.title: Game speed limits
perf.gameSupplies: The game rules, a driver and the limits.

phone-mode.mechanics: none: app shell and device support
phone-mode.use: The game has a phone layout: layout choice, fit zoom, safe areas, the one bottom sheet, second-tap commit.
phone-mode.not: Desktop-only games; some owners skip phone.
phone-mode.title: Phone screen layout
phone-mode.looks: A phone-sized layout with one bottom sheet and a second tap to confirm.
phone-mode.gameSupplies: The layouts, breakpoints and the sheet content.

picked-state.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
picked-state.use: Marking an option the player has picked, as tokens plus a helper.
picked-state.title: Marks on picked options
picked-state.looks: A visible mark on options the player has chosen.
picked-state.gameSupplies: The look tokens for a picked option.

pieces-3d.use: Dice, balls and chips built in code with WebGL or CSS (no model files); a round transparent token chip with die cut edge, no rectangle behind it, its shadow follows the outline; a die-cut token as a true extruded 3D solid (outline traced from the scan alpha, real mm size, back face, side walls, tilt and turn); a round hollow (recess, crevice) sunk into a disc token's front face, with its own wall and floor.
pieces-3d.not: Modelled or generated meshes; the owner does no 3D model work.
pieces-3d.title: Dice, balls and chips in 3D
pieces-3d.looks: Rounded dice, a rolling ball, a thick chip and an extruded die-cut token with a cast shadow.
pieces-3d.gameSupplies: The look: colours, faces and sizes.

pieces-3d-verbs.use: Release 1.1: the shake, flip, move and settle verbs for pieces-3d dice and balls, over the effect library.
pieces-3d-verbs.not: Drawing the pieces (pieces-3d); a 1.0 game never pulls it.
pieces-3d-verbs.title: Roll, shake and flip for 3D pieces
pieces-3d-verbs.looks: Dice and balls shake, flip, travel and settle.
pieces-3d-verbs.gameSupplies: The dice or balls and the effect library.

plain-text.mechanics: none: shows or checks text on screen
plain-text.use: Every line a person reads must be free of rule ids (`TURN-07`, `AR-12`).
plain-text.title: Keep rule ids off the screen
plain-text.gameSupplies: The words to show, free of ids.

plan-checker.use: Checking a game plan and listing a batch's line ranges (`plancheck.py --batch`); explicit strict applicability supports non-card plans while retaining rule, scenario, session and reuse checks.
plan-checker.not: Anything but the plan file format.
plan-checker.title: Check a build plan document

play-stats.use: Records of finished games, totals, best scores and a play-time clock.
play-stats.title: Records and totals of finished games

player-board.use: A mat with named zones from a layout: each zone fits its cards (largest size, two rows, a fan below the readable minimum) and is a motion anchor; a pure plan plus a React board with slots the game fills.
player-board.not: Where zones sit (the game's layout), card faces, tucked attachments (K245), piles.
player-board.title: Player mat with card zones
player-board.looks: A mat divided into named areas, each fitting its cards.
player-board.gameSupplies: The layout of zones and the cards in each.

prompt-gallery.use: Showing one state per prompt kind and ending, with a check that no kind lacks one.
prompt-gallery.title: Gallery of every question and ending
prompt-gallery.looks: A developer page showing one example screen for every kind of question.
prompt-gallery.gameSupplies: One state per prompt kind and per ending.

proof-sheet.mechanics: none: content tooling (art, scans, card data)
proof-sheet.use: Review a pack’s faces beside fields, printed words, generated words and flags, with filters in the hash and a static export.
proof-sheet.not: Designing faces, loading packs or deciding which findings a game should flag.
proof-sheet.title: Review sheet of card faces and fields
proof-sheet.looks: Cards shown beside their data, printed words and warning flags.
proof-sheet.gameSupplies: The pack with card faces and the field list.

prompt-host.use: Showing the open engine-core prompt on screen: a widget per prompt kind (a missing one fails to compile), the common widgets (pick, amount, order, may, pay) unstyled, forced answers sent from the store in one undo step (answerWithForced), board picks with tap to confirm (one or several). Recipe: docs/recipes/prompts.md.
prompt-host.not: The game's look or its own kind-specific widgets; board highlights (the game draws those from the option ids).
prompt-host.title: Question box
prompt-host.looks: The box that asks the player a question, with a widget for each kind of question.
prompt-host.gameSupplies: A widget for each prompt kind, and the look.
hooks: useBoardPick: board pick confirmation that yields keyboard input to dialogs

prompt-source.use: Each prompt must name its source card and clause and who decides.
prompt-source.title: Which card and clause asked the question
prompt-source.looks: A line naming the card and clause that caused a question.
prompt-source.gameSupplies: The source card and clause on each prompt.

reference-game.use: Kit CI only: generated card and solo tactical references whose own checks verify shared compositions, delayed semantic oracles, paired hidden worlds, combat/exploration, save/replay and source failure controls.
reference-game.not: Pulling into a game or copying as a starter; use scaffold for a new game.
reference-game.title: Tiny sample game that tests the kit
reference-game.gameSupplies: Nothing; it is for kit checks only.
reference-game.exports: `reference.test.ts`, `expedition.test.ts`; canonical scaffold card/courier overlays and separate expedition overlay

replay-cli.use: Headless replays, golden games and a determinism check across two checkouts.
replay-cli.title: Replay saved games from the command line
replay-cli.gameSupplies: The game rules and the golden games.

repo-gate.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
repo-gate.use: A repository gate for file sizes, staged dependency links, secrets, session URLs, runner names, card ids in rules code and art budgets.
repo-gate.title: Repository safety check
repo-gate.gameSupplies: The limits and the scan lists in its config file.

resolution-frame.mechanics: none: app shell and device support
resolution-frame.use: A Resolution setting that lays out for a chosen screen size and scales to the window.
resolution-frame.title: Screen-size setting
resolution-frame.looks: The whole table scales to fit the window, with bars at the sides if needed.
resolution-frame.gameSupplies: The list of screen sizes and the table to scale.

character-select.use: A pick-your-character screen before a game: roster by set, hero with portrait and summary, deck browser, opponent strip, modes, folded options and Begin; the game supplies data, slots and look.
character-select.not: The game's own board or track (pass it in the track slot) or building its new-game options.
character-select.title: Pick-your-character screen
character-select.looks: A screen with a roster of heroes, portrait, deck browser and a Begin button.
character-select.gameSupplies: The roster, decks, modes and slots.

controls.mechanics: none: a way to point or pick on screen
controls.use: Segmented, Toggle, Slider and TextField as plain behaviour parts that a game skins by data-part, replacing native selects, checkboxes and range inputs.
controls.not: A game look, or form layout and validation.
controls.title: Basic form controls
controls.looks: A segmented choice, an on-off switch, a slider and a text box with no style of their own.

rules-screen.mechanics: none: shows or checks text on screen
rules-screen.use: Show a game-owned rulebook with contents, ranked search, glossary links, annotated diagrams and reference sheets.
rules-screen.not: Engine rules or deciding printed wording; the game owns the book and its assets.
rules-screen.title: In-game rulebook
rules-screen.looks: A readable rulebook with contents, search, links and diagrams.
rules-screen.gameSupplies: The rulebook text, diagrams and glossary.

saves.use: Saved games in IndexedDB over engine-core's save file and a saves screen.
saves.not: Old-save migration work (the owner's rule: none until the game is complete).
saves.title: Saved games and their screen
saves.looks: A list of saved games to load, rename or delete.
saves.gameSupplies: The game state type and the screen look.

scaffold.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
scaffold.use: Start an empty working game repo, or generate a pinned executable courier or bounded card composition from a declarative specification. Run its declared non-browser checks and separate Chromium acceptance.
scaffold.not: Anything inside a running game; it is a generator run from the kit checkout.
scaffold.title: Start a new game project
scaffold.gameSupplies: The game id/name; for an executable composition, its approved supported records, independent rules and setup.
scaffold.exports: `node kit.mjs new <dir> <id> "<Name>"`, `node kit.mjs spec resolve|generate`, `scaffold(options)` in scaffold.js

scaffold/spec.title: Declarative game starter
scaffold/spec.use: Resolve component profiles and generate a pinned, retryable local scaffold from a game specification.

scaffold/courier.title: Playable courier assembly
scaffold/courier.use: Generate the original courier rules, store, public-view UI and simulation from a pinned, bounded configuration; wire its strict non-card plan, executable rule inventory, text and theme gates. Execute the generated acceptance before claiming the game slice passed.

scan-ingest.mechanics: none: content tooling (art, scans, card data)
scan-ingest.use: Turning flatbed scans into one cropped upright image per item; a printed board scan with live state drawn into its boxes, die-cut pieces at true size, playmat box detection, tone profile.
scan-ingest.not: Scanning crew boards. Offline scan tools prepare assets. ScanBoard and Piece are available in-game.
scan-ingest.title: Turn scans into cropped pictures
scan-ingest.gameSupplies: The scan files and the crop settings.
scan-ingest.exports: Python package `scanpipe`; TS `index.ts` (measureBoxes, planOverlay, clipPathOf, mmStyle, uniformOutlines...), `ui.ts` (ScanBoard, Piece)
hooks: loadGeometry: load scan board geometry, retry a failed attempt and cache successful measurements

screens.use: Main menu and new-game set-up form (seats, scenario, difficulty, extras) from data, unstyled, with a pure default and validate. Non-table screen frame, footer, disclaimer and persistent theme toggle.
screens.not: Styled or game-specific screens, or settings (use settings).
screens.title: Main menu and new-game form
screens.looks: A main menu and a set-up form with seats, scenario and difficulty.
screens.gameSupplies: The menu entries and the set-up fields.
hooks: MainMenu: the main menu
SetupForm + defaultSetup + validateSetup: the new game set-up form and its check
ScreenFrame: frame for settings, saves and rules screens
createThemeStore + ThemeToggle: light and dark theme switch
Footer + disclaimer: the footer line

settings.mechanics: none: app shell and device support
settings.use: Settings declared as data, a persisted store and a screen drawn from them.
settings.not: Game rules options that change the engine (declare them as settings, read them in setup).
settings.title: Settings store and screen
settings.looks: A settings page built from a list of options, remembered between visits.
settings.gameSupplies: The setting definitions, words and sections.

dev-autoplay.use: A dev-only URL flag (?dev=1&autoplay=<prompt kind>[*n], steps=N, seat=S) that plays the game store with a sim-pool bot until the open prompt is of that kind, then stops so the developer lands on that screen; off in production builds.
dev-autoplay.not: Playing for the player in a release, or animating the bot (it answers at once).
dev-autoplay.title: Jump to a screen by auto-playing
dev-autoplay.gameSupplies: The game store and a bot.

sim-pool.use: Playing many whole games with drivers on worker threads, fuzzing, sanity bands, sweeps, the K200 weight tuner and paired validation; the whole-game check of unreached clauses (proof from counted full-resolve tests, with a trace input built from the game's own log so a static clause applied with an effect counts as proven), coverage rounds and a findings file to replay a failing seed; K737 random debug edits (randomDebug hook, debug N) applied every N actions in a fuzz run, and a driver or hasten returning a debug action. Validate public seat views as JSON, detect hidden information leaks, and check registered driver names before a batch runs.
sim-pool.not: Strategy beyond one nested public choice (the game or opponent supplies it).
sim-pool.title: Bulk game simulator
sim-pool.gameSupplies: The game rules and a driver for each seat.
hooks: simGame: the module that plays one game for the pool
runGames: play many whole games on worker threads
fuzzMain: fuzz games with invariants and report each finding with a seed
randomDriver + legalAnswers: random answers from the legal options
botDriver: a driver that sees the player view only
runResumable + codeVersion: a long run that resumes after a crash
tune + validate: tune weights, then check on fresh seeds
proveResolved + provenClauses: prove each clause resolved in a played game
dispatchTrace: count a clause resolved only when verb dispatch ran it, not in a dry run
greedyBot + greedyPreview: score legal moves with bounded public nested look-ahead and a legal fallback

sim-pool/greedy.title: Simple public-view AI opponent
sim-pool/greedy.use: Play against the computer, choose the best legal move, or let a bot pick a legal action with bounded engine previews and a public fallback. Use greedyBot and greedyPreview from sim-pool/browser.ts for live play and sim-pool/index.ts for simulation.

small-helpers.mechanics: none: small helpers with no rule in them
small-helpers.use: Icon with hidden word, text-key check, paired legality fixtures, relation index, base-aware asset paths, plural and number formats.
small-helpers.title: Small pure helper functions
small-helpers.gameSupplies: Depends on the helper; see its entry.

sound-player.use: Release 1.2 sound and music from one data table on Web Audio.
sound-player.title: Sound and music player
sound-player.gameSupplies: The table of sounds and the audio files.
hooks: createSoundPlayer: one player for every sound, voice and music cue, from a table
play: play a sound cue by name
playTrack: play background music
stopCues: fade a sound out early, never a hard stop
unlock: let sound start after the first tap
setVolumes: change music, sound and voice volume from the settings
onEnd: run something when a sound ends, fades or is dropped
canPlay: ask whether a cue can sound
checkSoundFiles: check every sound file exists, its format and size

state-machines.mechanics: none: small helpers with no rule in them
state-machines.use: Naming a screen or flow state explicitly as a table instead of scattered flags.
state-machines.title: Named screen states
state-machines.gameSupplies: The table of states and moves.

story.use: Story, flavour text, panels and splash as data that never blocks play.
story.title: Story and flavour text panels
story.looks: Story panels and a splash screen that never block play.

table-panels.mechanics: none: draws what the engine or the game decided
table-panels.use: The panels around the table, unstyled: log (event words with slots, by turn, seat filter), banner (turn, seat, phase, fires on change), game over (result, breakdown slot, rematch, review log, home), opponent turn (paced-view steps, what the viewer may see, skip to end).
table-panels.not: Any look, layout or game text; the log data itself (game-log); the opponent's decisions (opponent).
table-panels.title: Log, turn banner and game-over panels
tags: game log whole lines no cut line
table-panels.looks: The log, the turn banner, the opponent-turn notice and the game-over panel.

target-arrow.mechanics: none: a way to point or pick on screen
target-arrow.use: A curved targeting arrow from the card that asks to the pointer: snaps to legal targets, collapses into the chosen one, then a hit; holds token flights until the hit.
target-arrow.not: Prompt kinds, which prompts are targets, the prompt panel (prompt-host) or the arrow's colours.
target-arrow.title: Arrow from a card to its target
target-arrow.looks: A curved arrow from the card to the pointer that snaps to a legal target.
target-arrow.gameSupplies: The card, the legal targets and the look.

theme-check.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
theme-check.use: Checking that the game's look lives in its token file, fonts and layout, and one dev page (Sheet) showing every registered component or view with its states and a hash filter.
theme-check.not: Choosing the look; the director's wireframes and themes do that.
theme-check.title: Check that the look lives in tokens
theme-check.gameSupplies: The token file, fonts and layout.

token-bag.use: A bag of tokens with its count; the engine's draw shown as a 2D flight from the bag or a 3D shake-and-draw (three.js by dynamic import) that never decides the draw and falls back to 2D; a finite supply of pieces counted from the engine's integers (supply.ts); finite stocks and a bag for the engine (stock.ts, pure): each piece in one named place, a gain from a stock that runs out says so, a seeded draw of N with the game's short-bag rule per kind of draw (draw what is left, refill when the bag runs out, or fail).
token-bag.not: Which tokens are drawn (the engine), the token faces and the bag print (the game), a game's token tables.
token-bag.title: Bag of tokens with a draw
token-bag.looks: A bag with a count; a token flies out or the bag shakes in 3D.
token-bag.gameSupplies: The tokens, their count and the draw result.
hooks: TokenBag + draw: show a token drawn from a bag, in 2D or 3D, after the engine drew it
onDrawDone: clear the draw when the flight ended
assignDraws: which token rises comes from the drawn kinds only
placeTokens: tokens in a finite box, short as a badge
makeStocks: finite stocks and a bag in the engine state

token-flights.use: Tokens that moved between two views fly from where they were to where they are, with a ledger that draws each token in one place at a time.
token-flights.not: Cards flying, motion specs (motion-frame) or the token look.
token-flights.title: Tokens fly between places
token-flights.looks: Tokens glide from where they were to where they are now.
token-flights.gameSupplies: The views before and after, and the token elements.

art-pipeline.mechanics: none: content tooling (art, scans, card data)
art-pipeline.use: Game-free scripts for a card game's art, driven by the game's config: an index of one chosen image per card (order, overrides, degraded rule), fetch with sha256, sheet cells and crops, PDF pages as faces, a CI cache keyed on input hashes, publish to public with a manifest art-check reads, with a minimum JPEG quality within a size cap and an enlarged-face check.
art-pipeline.not: Mapping card ids to files, the sources' URLs and parsing a dossier: those stay in the game and go in as config.
art-pipeline.title: Get card art ready for the game
art-pipeline.gameSupplies: The art config: sources, ids and output.
hooks: art-publish: publish art with filename collision checks and recover interrupted replacement

tooling-scripts.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
tooling-scripts.use: Small repo scripts run with `node kit/tooling-scripts/<script>.ts` (art check, shots, text-leak, home screen, docs index). Recipe: docs/recipes/agent-workflow.md.
tooling-scripts.title: Small command-line tool scripts
tooling-scripts.gameSupplies: Each script takes its own paths and flags.
hooks: art-check: check the output manifest against sources and independently required logical art ids

traceability.use: Test titles must cite the game's rule ids; gate configured in `trace.config.json`.
traceability.not: Showing ids on screen (plain-text forbids it).
traceability.title: Tests must cite rule ids

traceability/assertions.title: Executable rule evidence
traceability/assertions.use: Run arbiter fixtures and check that every due rule has passing setup or action evidence.

track.use: A row of spaces with a marker that glides (drawn row or spots on a mat image), per-space marks, labels from the game's words; a hop-and-fill bar with a badge pop; a step list with one lit step; unstyled.
track.not: Any rule, look, colour or word; turn banners (table-panels); the number itself (counter).
track.title: Track with a moving marker
track.looks: A row of spaces with a marker that glides along it.
track.gameSupplies: The spaces, marker position and look.

transcription-check.mechanics: none: content tooling (art, scans, card data)
transcription-check.use: Printed items (cards, tiles, boards) are transcribed twice independently and the owner verifies them before they enter the real pack; also the face fit check (printed text fits its box at a pixel floor) and Python tools to measure, fit, autotune and crop-sheet faces.
transcription-check.not: Card rules or card-language checks (card-harness); anything that reads no files.
transcription-check.title: Double-checked card transcription
transcription-check.gameSupplies: The two transcriptions and the item list.

tutorial.use: A scripted tutorial on a seed with the lock that allows only the scripted answer.
tutorial.title: Scripted tutorial on a fixed game
tutorial.gameSupplies: The script, the seed and the phase table.

ui-helpers.mechanics: none: small helpers with no rule in them
ui-helpers.use: Small screen helpers: hover hold, inspect, rule sheet, toasts, prompt keys. For an engine-core prompt use prompt-host instead of createSelection and onlyForcedAnswer.
ui-helpers.title: Small screen helper functions
ui-helpers.gameSupplies: Depends on the helper; see its entry.
hooks: bindPromptKeys + bindPlayKeys: background keyboard shortcuts and prompt keys that pause under a dialog
activeOverlay: find the active overlay keyboard owner

voice.use: Release 1.3 voice lines on the sound player's voice bus, never twice the same.
voice.title: Spoken lines player
voice.gameSupplies: The voice lines and the gate for when to play.

turn-flow.use: Rounds, turns per seat in seat order, and phases and steps inside a turn as one data table; the runner calls engine-core boundary() at each turn, phase and round edge, so endOfTurn / endOfRound / endOfPhase durations end with no manual call; whoseTurn and flowOf read the position from state; a skipped turn, phase or step can say why (K729: skip returns { by, why }, the runner emits a skipped event naming the card, so a log says why a phase was skipped); once-per limits (K589: once per turn, round, phase or game, per card, per seat) bar a used option with its reason and clear at the matching edge. Recipe: docs/recipes/turn-flow.md.
turn-flow.not: What a step does, simultaneous or out-of-order turns (interrupts, reactions), step-long durations (engine-core has none), or the screen that shows the phase.
turn-flow.title: Rounds, turns and phases table
turn-flow.gameSupplies: The table of rounds, turns, phases and steps.
hooks: FlowConfig + flowHandlers + startFlow: rounds, turns and phases from one table
endTurn: end a turn early, pass
flowOf + whoseTurn: whose turn it is and which phase
skip: skip a turn or a phase
roundEnds + over: end the round and end the game
LimitTable + limitOption + markLimit: once per turn, once per round or once per game
expireEffects: drop effects that ended at the end of a turn, phase or round

app-icons.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
app-icons.use: Generate opaque home-screen icons and a relative web manifest from game-owned art.
app-icons.not: Creating artwork or choosing a game’s visual identity.
app-icons.title: Home-screen icons and manifest

llm-playtester.use: Headless whole-game playtests by Claude through a small game adapter (view, numbered options, choose): finds rules and screen bugs the model flags, adapter throws and illegal option lists, and saves each run's replay for a replay test; capped in dollars per run; --dummy plays the first option for free. Cheap by default: prompt caching, a single option taken without a call, multi-select and split-points questions answered in one call, --effort low, and a cached reference() lookup table of card texts.
llm-playtester.not: The in-game Claude opponent (a game's own server code) or balance sims at volume; use sim-pool for many cheap games.
llm-playtester.title: Whole-game playtests by Claude
llm-playtester.gameSupplies: An adapter: view, numbered options and choose.

check-runner/receipts.title: Acceptance receipts bound to source and inputs
check-runner/receipts.use: Record the existing full check plan's commands and outcomes with consumer, kit lock, specification and acceptance-definition fingerprints; reject stale, missing, stopped, truncated or unfinished local evidence. Does not certify test quality or authenticate execution.

plan-checker/applicability.title: Strict checks for non-card game plans
plan-checker/applicability.use: Declare whether card encoding and LLM playtesting apply, with reasons and contradiction checks; validate real rule and scenario inventories without legacy optional flags. Default plans retain the existing card requirements.

card-harness/mutations.title: Semantic mutation tests for card clauses
card-harness/mutations.use: Run a game's original spec rows against altered card records, check an independent inventory of printed clauses, and fail the content gate on invalid, crashing, or surviving mutants and missing tests.

engine-core/timing.title: Prevention, replacement and triggers
engine-core/timing.use: An effect can be prevented, replaced or answered by others: batches of occurrences, the prevention window, the replacement loop, triggers.

engine-core/lasting-effects.title: Lasting effects and durations
engine-core/lasting-effects.use: An effect stays for a while and changes numbers or rules until a boundary or a named event the game fires ends it (`addEffect`, `boundary`, `eventOver`, `waitingOn`, `effectsOf`, `sumEffects`).

engine-core/layers.title: Layers for continuous effects
engine-core/layers.use: Several lasting effects change the same thing and the order matters (`layered`, `stampActive`).

engine-core/legal.title: Legal moves and reasons
engine-core/legal.use: The game says which options are legal, bars the others with a reason code, and notices the only option (`bar`, `blocked`, `onlyOne`, `legalTable`); the only legal answer is taken automatically (`askOrTake`) unless the player has not seen it (`unseen`: a hidden or face-down option is asked).

engine-core/preview.title: Outcome preview
engine-core/preview.use: Show or test what an answer would do before it is given, stopping at hidden information (`preview`).

engine-core/do-nothing.title: Options that do nothing
engine-core/do-nothing.use: Find or mark an option whose effect would change nothing (`doesNothing`, `idleProblems`, `markIdle`).

card-language/verb-pack.title: Standard verb pack
card-language/verb-pack.use: Card effects use the common verbs (draw, discard, move, gain, pay, choose and the rest) instead of game-written ones.

card-language/triggers.title: Triggers printed on cards
card-language/triggers.use: A card prints "when X, do Y": `when` on card data, compiled by `cardTriggers` into the engine's triggers.

card-language/op-table.title: Op table for a game on its own engine
card-language/op-table.use: A game that keeps its own engine still wants one row per op with checked fields, a run function and its text (`OpTable`, `runOp`, `validateOps`).

card-language/payment-plans.title: Substitutable resource payment plans
card-language/payment-plans.use: Enumerate minimal ways to pay from a shared pool with substitutions and required holdings (`paymentPlans`), or rank affordable plans with a game-owned policy (`preferredPayment`).

clock.use: A marker on a row of spaces as rules data (countdown, round tracker, danger or doom track): steps forward or back by the game's number, thresholds that fire on landing or passing (lose, trigger, reward, limit) in order, once-only thresholds, per-space values such as a limit read from the marker's row; a lose space anywhere on the row, on landing or on passing; crossings become engine-core occurrences that can carry the threshold's data and space.
clock.not: Drawing the track (track); turn or round flow (turn-flow); deciding what a threshold does (the game); tokens counted without a cap, with no fixed row of spaces (a counter in the game).
clock.title: Clock or countdown with thresholds
clock.gameSupplies: The spaces, start, direction, thresholds with their kinds and data, and per-space values.
hooks: newClock: a marker on a track of spaces
step: move the marker and get the thresholds it met
setTo: place the marker without firing anything
stepsTo: the steps to reach a space on the track
ended + reached: the marker reached the end or a space
overrun: the marker cannot advance, no space left
occurrences: thresholds as engine events for triggers
valueAt: a limit that depends on the marker space
checkClock: check a track spec in a content test

picture-upscale.use: Making a picture bigger without blur (2-4x) offline on the GPU with a super-resolution model, for art shown larger than its source.
picture-upscale.not: Resizing in the browser, generating new art, or diffusion upscalers (SeedVR2, SUPIR).
picture-upscale.title: Enlarge a picture with a model
picture-upscale.gameSupplies: The source pictures, the output folder and the target scale or width.
picture-upscale.exports: CLI `upscale.py` (run, check, status, fetch), see its README

worker-rules.mechanics: none: build, CI or repository tooling
worker-rules.use: The one block of worker rules from the kit that every game's agents file (AGENTS.md) carries: kit first, Must use is an order, Kit gap needs proof, no deciding rules or looks, caps, report order. `pull` stamps it between markers; `worker-rules --adopt` lists hand-written copies to remove.
worker-rules.not: A game never edits the stamped text or pulls this component; its own rules go outside the markers.
worker-rules.title: Worker rules block
worker-rules.gameSupplies: Its own lines in AGENTS.md outside the markers.

guarded-button.use: A danger button that needs two taps: tap one lifts a guard, tap two fires; closes on timeout, Escape or a tap elsewhere; a barred state with its reason; unstyled.
guarded-button.not: A dialog or backdrop (modal-dialog); the board second-tap commit (phone-mode, prompt-host); the guard look.
guarded-button.title: Guarded two-tap button
guarded-button.looks: A danger button under a hinged guard that lifts on the first tap.
guarded-button.gameSupplies: The label, the look of the button and its guard.

cheat-options.use: Dev cheats a game declares as data at set-up (number or toggle; once at set-up or every round start), applied only as recorded debug set edits behind allowCheats, with set-up form fields and a cheated mark.
cheat-options.not: Debug edits typed by hand (debug-console) or rigging a sim deck or hand.
cheat-options.title: Cheat options at set-up
cheat-options.gameSupplies: The cheat list (paths and amounts) and the options that hold the choice.
hooks: CheatDef + cheatActions: cheats as data, applied as debug edits
cheatFields + cheatsFrom: the set-up form fields
cheatedOf + cheatProblem: the cheated mark and the set-up check

visual-replay.mechanics: none: playback presentation over recorded engine actions
visual-replay.use: Watch a recorded game on its own table with action and turn navigation.
visual-replay.not: Headless determinism checks (replay-cli) or saving games (saves).
visual-replay.title: Watch a recorded game
visual-replay.gameSupplies: The recording adapter, engine, player view, boundaries and table.
visual-replay.looks: The game table shows recorded actions with playback controls.

reference-game/campaign-continuation.title: Playable campaign continuation reference
reference-game/campaign-continuation.use: Prove ordered calendar choices, attendance/retirement, shared-copy deck exchanges, live save/restore and retry in two original four-card campaign configurations.
